shorts.title: What you will learn: protected and access control
shorts.hook: Protected is for the family only.
shorts.script: Protected is for the family only. Today we meet the third access label. It sits between public and private, and it is made for inheritance. Public members are open to everyone. Private members are open to the class only. Protected members are open to the class and to its derived classes, but not to the outside. Choose the strictest label that works. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: protected and access control.

shorts.title: protected and access control in one minute
shorts.hook: Public members are open to everyone.
shorts.script: Public members are open to everyone. Private members are open to the class only. Protected members are open to the class and to its derived classes, but not to the outside. Choose the strictest label that works. Think of a family house. The street sees the gate. The family sees the hall. Only you see your own room. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: PROTECTED AND ACCESS CONTROL IN ONE MINUTE
shorts.caption: protected and access control in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Open is public. Everyone can read it. Family is protected. Secret is private. A public getter lets others read the secret. The child adds all three parts. It reads family directly, and secret through the getter. The sum is six. Main may read the public part. The program prints six, and then one. Public is open to everyone. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Reaching protected data from outside
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. Main reads a protected member. The compiler says the balance is protected within this context. Protected is open to children, not to outside code. Add a public getter. Protected members are for the class and its children. Main is outside code, so it cannot reach them. Public is open to everyone. Protected is open to the class and its children. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: REACHING PROTECTED DATA FROM OUTSIDE
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Reaching protected data from outside.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Protected is the middle child of access labels. It always gets along with the family.
shorts.script: Protected is the middle child of access labels. It always gets along with the family. Write a class with a name, an id and a secret code. Decide which label each one needs, and explain in a comment. Write your answer in the comments. Public is open to everyone. Protected is open to the class and its children. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
